cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
cwes.summary: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the path

cwes.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwes.summary: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.

cwes.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
cwes.summary: The product constructs all or part of a code segment using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the syntax or behavior of the intend

cwes.name: Missing Authorization
cwes.summary: The product does not perform an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.

cwes.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
cwes.summary: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

cwes.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
cwes.summary: The product does not properly control the allocation and maintenance of a limited resource.

cwes.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwes.summary: The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
cwes.summary: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is se

cwes.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.summary: The product does not perform any authentication for functionality that requires a provable user identity or consumes a significant amount of resources.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.summary: The product exposes sensitive information to an actor that is not explicitly authorized to have access to that information.

cwes.name: Improper Input Validation
cwes.summary: The product receives input or data, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties that are required to process the data safely and correctly.

cwes.name: Incorrect Authorization
cwes.summary: The product performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action, but it does not correctly perform the check.

cwes.name: Improper Access Control
cwes.summary: The product does not restrict or incorrectly restricts access to a resource from an unauthorized actor.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
cwes.summary: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

cwes.name: Improper Authentication
cwes.summary: When an actor claims to have a given identity, the product does not prove or insufficiently proves that the claim is correct.

cwes.name: Origin Validation Error
cwes.summary: The product does not properly verify that the source of data or communication is valid.

cwes.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
cwes.summary: The product allocates a reusable resource or group of resources on behalf of an actor without imposing any intended restrictions on the size or number of resources that can be allocated.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
cwes.summary: The product constructs all or part of a command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended command when it is sent to a

cwes.name: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs
cwes.summary: The product implements a protection mechanism that relies on a list of inputs (or properties of inputs) that are not allowed by policy or otherwise require other action to neutralize before additional processing takes place, but the list is

cwes.name: Reachable Assertion
cwes.summary: The product contains an assert() or similar statement that can be triggered by an attacker, which leads to an application exit or other behavior that is more severe than necessary.

cwes.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
cwes.summary: The product does not use or incorrectly uses a protection mechanism that provides sufficient defense against directed attacks against the product.

cwes.name: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
cwes.summary: The product does not release or incorrectly releases a resource before it is made available for re-use.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
cwes.summary: The product constructs all or part of a command, data structure, or record using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify how it is pars

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.summary: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is

cwes.name: Out-of-bounds Read
cwes.summary: The product reads data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

cwes.name: Improper Validation of Array Index
cwes.summary: The product uses untrusted input when calculating or using an array index, but the product does not validate or incorrectly validates the index to ensure the index references a valid position within the array.

cwes.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
cwes.summary: The product contains a concurrent code sequence that requires temporary, exclusive access to a shared resource, but a timing window exists in which the shared resource can be modified by another code sequence operating concurrently.

cwes.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
cwes.summary: The product attempts to access a file based on the filename, but it does not properly prevent that filename from identifying a link or shortcut that resolves to an unintended resource.

cwes.name: External Control of File Name or Path
cwes.summary: The product allows user input to control or influence paths or file names that are used in filesystem operations.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
cwes.summary: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before using the input in a dynamic evaluation call (e.g. eval).

cwes.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
cwes.summary: The product checks the state of a resource before using that resource, but the resource's state can change between the check and the use in a way that invalidates the results of the check.

cwes.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
cwes.summary: The product does not sufficiently track and release allocated memory after it has been used, making the memory unavailable for reallocation and reuse.

cwes.name: Insufficient Session Expiration
cwes.summary: According to WASC, Insufficient Session Expiration is when a web site permits an attacker to reuse old session credentials or session IDs for authorization.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
cwes.summary: The product generates a query intended to access or manipulate data in a data store such as a database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that can modify the intended logic of the query.

cwes.name: Relative Path Traversal
cwes.summary: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

cwes.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
cwes.summary: The product performs a calculation that can produce an integer overflow or wraparound when the logic assumes that the resulting value will always be larger than the original value. This occurs when an integer value is incremented to a value

cwes.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
cwes.summary: The product generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.

cwes.name: Incorrect Privilege Assignment
cwes.summary: A product incorrectly assigns a privilege to a particular actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

cwes.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwes.summary: The product uses a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm or protocol.

cwes.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.summary: The product does not sufficiently verify the origin or authenticity of data, in a way that causes it to accept invalid data.

cwes.name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwes.summary: The product transmits or stores authentication credentials, but it uses an insecure method that is susceptible to unauthorized interception and/or retrieval.

cwes.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
cwes.summary: The product writes sensitive information to a log file.

cwes.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cwes.summary: The product imports, requires, or includes executable functionality (such as a library) from a source that is outside of the intended control sphere.

cwes.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
cwes.summary: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.

cwes.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
cwes.summary: The product uses a regular expression with a worst-case computational complexity that is inefficient and possibly exponential.

cwes.name: Absolute Path Traversal
cwes.summary: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that direc

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
cwes.summary: The product constructs a string for a command to be executed by a separate component in another control sphere, but it does not properly delimit the intended arguments, options, or switches within that command string.

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
cwes.summary: The product performs operations on a memory buffer, but it reads from or writes to a memory location outside the buffer's intended boundary. This may result in read or write operations on unexpected memory locations that could be linked to

cwes.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
cwes.summary: The code transmits data to another actor, but a portion of the data includes sensitive information that should not be accessible to that actor.

cwes.name: Uncaught Exception
cwes.summary: An exception is thrown from a function, but it is not caught.

cwes.name: Improper Privilege Management
cwes.summary: The product does not properly assign, modify, track, or check privileges for an actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

cwes.name: Improper Authorization
cwes.summary: The product does not perform or incorrectly performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.

cwes.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
cwes.summary: The product stores sensitive information in cleartext within a resource that might be accessible to another control sphere.

cwes.name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.summary: The product transmits sensitive or security-critical data in cleartext in a communication channel that can be sniffed by unauthorized actors.

cwes.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')
cwes.summary: The product uses external input with reflection to select which classes or code to use, but it does not sufficiently prevent the input from selecting improper classes or code.

cwes.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
cwes.summary: The product dereferences a pointer that it expects to be valid but is NULL.

cwes.name: .NET Misconfiguration: Use of Impersonation
cwes.summary: Allowing a .NET application to run at potentially escalated levels of access to the underlying operating and file systems can be dangerous and result in various forms of attacks.

cwes.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.summary: The web application accepts a user-controlled input that specifies a link to an external site, and uses that link in a redirect.

cwes.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
cwes.summary: The product does not properly control the amount of recursion that takes place, consuming excessive resources, such as allocated memory or the program stack.

cwes.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.summary: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

cwes.name: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
cwes.summary: The product provides an Applications Programming Interface (API) or similar interface for interaction with external actors, but the interface includes a dangerous method or function that is not properly restricted.

cwes.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
cwes.summary: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

cwes.name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
cwes.summary: One or more system settings or configuration elements can be externally controlled by a user.

cwes.name: Improper Resolution of Path Equivalence
cwes.summary: The product is vulnerable to file system contents disclosure through path equivalence. Path equivalence involves the use of special characters in file and directory names. The associated manipulations are intended to generate multiple names

cwes.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
cwes.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow condition is a condition where the buffer being overwritten is allocated on the stack (i.e., is a local variable or, rarely, a parameter to a function).

cwes.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
cwes.summary: A heap overflow condition is a buffer overflow, where the buffer that can be overwritten is allocated in the heap portion of memory, generally meaning that the buffer was allocated using a routine such as malloc().

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences
cwes.summary: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as escape, meta, or control character sequences when they are sent to a downstream compo

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Wildcards or Matching Symbols
cwes.summary: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could be interpreted as wildcards or matching symbols when they are sent to a downstream component.

cwes.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize
cwes.summary: The product validates input before it is canonicalized, which prevents the product from detecting data that becomes invalid after the canonicalization step.

cwes.name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
cwes.summary: Two separate operations in a product require different amounts of time to complete, in a way that is observable to an actor and reveals security-relevant information about the state of the product, such as whether a particular operation was

cwes.name: Improper Check for Dropped Privileges
cwes.summary: The product attempts to drop privileges but does not check or incorrectly checks to see if the drop succeeded.

cwes.name: Unverified Ownership
cwes.summary: The product does not properly verify that a critical resource is owned by the proper entity.

cwes.name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
cwes.summary: The product requires authentication, but the product has an alternate path or channel that does not require authentication.

cwes.name: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
cwes.summary: This attack-focused weakness is caused by incorrectly implemented authentication schemes that are subject to spoofing attacks.

cwes.name: Improper Certificate Validation
cwes.summary: The product does not validate, or incorrectly validates, a certificate.

cwes.name: Authentication Bypass by Primary Weakness
cwes.summary: The authentication algorithm is sound, but the implemented mechanism can be bypassed as the result of a separate weakness that is primary to the authentication error.

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
cwes.summary: The product does not implement sufficient measures to prevent multiple failed authentication attempts within a short time frame.

cwes.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
cwes.summary: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

cwes.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
cwes.summary: The product stores or transmits sensitive data using an encryption scheme that is theoretically sound, but is not strong enough for the level of protection required.

cwes.name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
cwes.summary: The product uses a Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG) in a security context, but the PRNG's algorithm is not cryptographically strong.

cwes.name: Use of Less Trusted Source
cwes.summary: The product has two different sources of the same data or information, but it uses the source that has less support for verification, is less trusted, or is less resistant to attack.

cwes.name: Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution for a Security-Critical Action
cwes.summary: The product performs reverse DNS resolution on an IP address to obtain the hostname and make a security decision, but it does not properly ensure that the IP address is truly associated with the hostname.

cwes.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwes.summary: The web application does not, or cannot, sufficiently verify whether a request was intentionally provided by the user who sent the request, which could have originated from an unauthorized actor.

cwes.name: Insecure Temporary File
cwes.summary: Creating and using insecure temporary files can leave application and system data vulnerable to attack.

cwes.name: Session Fixation
cwes.summary: Authenticating a user, or otherwise establishing a new user session, without invalidating any existing session identifier gives an attacker the opportunity to steal authenticated sessions.

cwes.name: Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)
cwes.summary: The product does not properly control situations in which an adversary can cause the product to consume or produce excessive resources without requiring the adversary to invest equivalent work or otherwise prove authorization, i.e., the adv

cwes.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
cwes.summary: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles a compressed input with a very high compression ratio that produces a large output.

cwes.name: Double Free
cwes.summary: The product calls free() twice on the same memory address.

cwes.name: Use After Free
cwes.summary: The product reuses or references memory after it has been freed. At some point afterward, the memory may be allocated again and saved in another pointer, while the original pointer references a location somewhere within the new allocation.

cwes.name: Unprotected Alternate Channel
cwes.summary: The product protects a primary channel, but it does not use the same level of protection for an alternate channel.

cwes.name: Improper Protection of Alternate Path
cwes.summary: The product does not sufficiently protect all possible paths that a user can take to access restricted functionality or resources.

cwes.name: Interpretation Conflict
cwes.summary: Product A handles inputs or steps differently than Product B, which causes A to perform incorrect actions based on its perception of B's state.

cwes.name: Expected Behavior Violation
cwes.summary: A feature, API, or function does not perform according to its specification.

cwes.name: Non-exit on Failed Initialization
cwes.summary: The product does not exit or otherwise modify its operation when security-relevant errors occur during initialization, such as when a configuration file has a format error or a hardware security module (HSM) cannot be activated, which can c

cwes.name: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
cwes.summary: The code uses a cache that contains sensitive information, but the cache can be read by an actor outside of the intended control sphere.

cwes.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
cwes.summary: The product places sensitive information into files or directories that are accessible to actors who are allowed to have access to the files, but not to the sensitive information.

cwes.name: Missing Standardized Error Handling Mechanism
cwes.summary: The product does not use a standardized method for handling errors throughout the code, which might introduce inconsistent error handling and resultant weaknesses.

cwes.name: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
cwes.summary: The product makes files or directories accessible to unauthorized actors, even though they should not be.

cwes.name: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere
cwes.summary: The product uses an externally controlled name or reference that resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources
cwes.summary: The product constructs the name of a file or other resource using input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the resulting name.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
cwes.summary: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XPath expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input. This allows an attacker to control the structure of t

cwes.name: Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres
cwes.summary: The product does not properly transfer a resource/behavior to another sphere, or improperly imports a resource/behavior from another sphere, in a manner that provides unintended control over that resource.

cwes.name: Incorrect Behavior Order
cwes.summary: The product performs multiple related behaviors, but the behaviors are performed in the wrong order in ways that may produce resultant weaknesses.

cwes.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
cwes.summary: The product does not check or incorrectly checks for unusual or exceptional conditions that are not expected to occur frequently during day to day operation of the product.

cwes.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
cwes.summary: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

cwes.name: Incomplete Filtering of Special Elements
cwes.summary: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

cwes.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwes.summary: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

cwes.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
cwes.summary: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of an input, but the input can be modified by an untrusted actor in a way that bypasses the protection mechanism.

cwes.name: Excessive Iteration
cwes.summary: The product performs an iteration or loop without sufficiently limiting the number of times that the loop is executed.

cwes.name: Use of Expired File Descriptor
cwes.summary: The product uses or accesses a file descriptor after it has been closed.

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
cwes.summary: The product establishes a communication channel to (or from) an endpoint for privileged or protected operations, but it does not properly ensure that it is communicating with the correct endpoint.

cwes.name: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default
cwes.summary: The product initializes or sets a resource with a default that is intended to be changed by the product's installer, administrator, or maintainer, but the default is not secure.

cwes.name: Hardware Child Block Incorrectly Connected to Parent System
cwes.summary: Signals between a hardware IP and the parent system design are incorrectly connected causing security risks.

cwes.name: Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address
cwes.summary: The product assigns the address 0.0.0.0 for a database server, a cloud service/instance, or any computing resource that communicates remotely.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
cwes.summary: The product uses a template engine to insert or process externally-influenced input, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements or syntax that can be interpreted as template expressions or other code directives w

cwes.name: Weak Authentication
cwes.summary: The product uses an authentication mechanism to restrict access to specific users or identities, but the mechanism does not sufficiently prove that the claimed identity is correct.
